verdict: 2026-07-29 11:39:10 PDT — I would keep the boolean-returning adapter, edge logging, pure retry reducer, and existing tick. I would not build rendering-context ownership this way: Show, Hide, and automatic recovery should pass through one serialized controller. No installed dependency already supplies this Zoom-specific lifecycle.

findings.title: Compensating close can destroy a newer Show
findings.claim: Generation checks detect stale recovery but do not serialize the global `runRenderingContext` and argument-free `closeRenderingContext` operations. If recovery is awaiting `start`, the presenter can Hide and then Show; when the stale start resolves, its compensating `stop` can close the newer Show's context. The final state is desired-on/UI-on with no live rendering context—the same invariant the redesign was meant to prevent.
findings.alternative: Introduce one small rendering-context controller or promise queue used by Show, Hide, camera recovery, and dead-link recovery. Record intent immediately, but serialize every SDK start/close; a Hide queued after an old start closes it, and a later Show is then the final operation. Keep the pure retry reducer as the controller's input.
findings.win: Eliminates the stale-close-after-new-Show error path and centralizes ordering for all rendering-context mutations instead of coordinating them across `generationRef`, `recoveringRef`, and compensating calls.
